head: 14b24dc09
rationale: N-4 as filed is CLOSED: the Exchange sender is now exactly microsoftexchange + 32 hex, and an Exchange-sender report is never entitled through a provider domain. Gitleaks clean, audit at high level exits 0, tests 47/47 and 40/40. FAIL remains because (1) the probe found one narrow residual of the same class, R-1 (LOW, conditional): on a Microsoft mailbox whose own From address is a consumer provider domain (e.g. me@hotmail.com), an Exchange-shaped sender at that same domain is still entitled through the exact sending-side match, which 14b24dc09 did not exclude; (2) H-1 (LOW, optional hardening) is still open; (3) pnpm audit --prod exits 1 on two pre-existing moderate advisories, and the rule is 'any finding at any severity is FAIL'. Nothing is CRITICAL or HIGH.

a_findings_introduced_by_pg207_still_ope.title: Exchange-shaped sender still entitled via the exact sending-side domain when the mailbox itself sends from a consumer provider domain
a_findings_introduced_by_pg207_still_ope.detail: 14b24dc09 empties only the provider list for exchangeSender reports. The sending-side exact match (mailbox From-address domain, smtpHost, imapHost) still applies. Probe: Microsoft mailbox me@hotmail.com, From MicrosoftExchange329e71ec88ae4615bbc36ab6ce41109e@hotmail.com with spf/dkim pass at hotmail.com, recipient v@victim.co.uk: ACT=true (N4c). Same sender at outlook.com for that mailbox: ACT=false. For a mailbox on a custom M365 domain, Exchange sender at outlook.com or hotmail.com: ACT=false (N4b), and postmaster@outlook.com still ACT=true (intended). So the N-4 hole is closed for custom-domain mailboxes and remains only for consumer-address mailboxes, and only if a consumer can register the public GUID name (not verified; Microsoft likely reserves it). Impact if it works: forged DSN naming a record's Message-ID and a co-recipient, causing a bounce/suppression for that co-recipient. Same class as OD-2 backscatter.
a_findings_introduced_by_pg207_still_ope.suggested_fix: In mayReportOn, when exchangeSender is true, drop sendingSide entries that are within any PROVIDER_REPORT_DOMAINS (or require speaksFor(reporter, recipientDomain) only, i.e. recipient's own domain, plus a non-provider sending-side match). Add a test: MICROSOFT mailbox with fromAddress at hotmail.com, Exchange-GUID sender at hotmail.com, other recipient -> no effect. Alternatively record the residual in ADR-085 as accepted.

a_findings_introduced_by_pg207_still_ope.title: No public-suffix guard
a_findings_introduced_by_pg207_still_ope.detail: Unchanged. Probe: a passing domain of co.uk speaks for victim.co.uk (ACT=true). No verifier reports a pass for a public suffix, so this is defence in depth only.

closed_since_previous_run.notes: bounce-senders.ts: EXCHANGE_SENDER_LOCAL_PART = /^microsoftexchange[0-9a-f]{32}$/i, anchored. Probes (gates/sec6-probe.txt): microsoftexchange, MicrosoftExchange1a2b, GUID+1 char, GUID-1 char, MicrosoftExchange + 32 non-hex: all unauthenticated, ACT=false. Microsoft mailbox on a custom domain, Exchange GUID sender at outlook.com / hotmail.com / microsoft.com / office365.com / sub.outlook.com, other recipient: ACT=false. Controls still behave: postmaster@outlook.com and mailer-daemon@hotmail.com ACT=true (provider-reserved, intended); Exchange GUID at the recipient's own domain ACT=true (genuine NDR); at an unrelated domain ACT=false. Previous Exchange look-alike set (Support, +tag, dotted, leading x, trailing space, quoted) all still ACT=false, as are no-auth, spf=fail, untrusted receiver and two-From cases. The flag is derived from the single validated From header in reportAuthentication (dsn-parser.ts:167,184), so it cannot be forged separately from the authenticated sender.

Diff reviewed: bounce-senders.ts, dsn-parser.ts (new exchangeSender field, returned in the none-case as false), bounce-reader.ts (extra arg to mayReportOn from entitledFor). oauth-mailbox.ts:487 still uses isBounceSenderAddress, which now rejects short/long Exchange forms: this narrows the Graph prefilter, no widening. No new dependency, secret, or input path.
